playbook:
When a pre-play notice says the others will punish anyone who contributes less than half in the first round, contribute 10 in round 1 to avoid triggering the punishment.

When there is no such notice and the others publicly promise full contributions, contribute 0 in round 1 to test whether they actually cooperate.

When the receipts from the group show everyone contributed 20 in a round (or show consistent high contributions), contribute 20 in the next round to reciprocate and keep the pot high.

When the receipts show someone cheated or contributed much less than promised (especially in early rounds), stop trusting unilateral cooperation: drop my contribution to 0 for the next round and only return to cooperation after I see at least one full round of everyone contributing.

When I am comfortably ahead of the others near the final rounds, contribute 0 to maximize my final payoff.

When I am behind near the end and need to catch up, increase my contribution (up to 20) if that is the only realistic way to change the ranking.

Always file a truthful receipt that equals the envelope amount I sealed; misreporting receipts is risky, harms trust, and did not reliably improve outcomes.

If I switch from 0 to 20 (or vice versa), communicate via receipts by matching the true amount so others can condition on my moves.

If I face uncertainty about others’ future behavior after one mixed round, lean on tit-for-tat: match the group's recent modal contribution (0 or 20) in the next round rather than randomizing.

When I want to sustain long-run cooperation for higher joint payoffs, be ready to reciprocate immediately after one round of unanimous high contributions.
